claim: ExeCRE estimates code reliability by statistical analysis of execution-output consistency over many random inputs using a Dawid-Skene latent-reliability model, and uses it to gate self-correction; under GPT-5.2 on LiveCodeBench misleading feedback on already-correct code drops from 113.2 to 14.0.
stance_target: L1/L3 execution-based reliability exists but is not calibration against ground truth
quoted_support: Under GPT-5.2 on LiveCodeBench, the average number of misleading feedback cases on already correct code drops from 113.2 with a representative self-correction baseline to 14.0 with ExeCRE.

claim: The evaluation applies explicit release-window versus knowledge-cutoff control: the 182-problem window is cutoff-clean for Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct (cutoff 2024-06) and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct (2023-12), but not for GPT-5.2 (2025-08); DeepSeek-V3.2 is unverifiable.
stance_target: L1 release-date contamination control is practised for pass@1 in self-correction work, not for confidence calibration
quoted_support: GPT-5.2, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct have reported knowledge cutoffs of 2025-08, 2024-06, and 2023-12, respectively.

claim: On cutoff-clean models ExeCRE raises Pass@1 modestly (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B 31.5 to 32.5; LLaMA-3.1-8B 19.4 to 21.0) while reducing misleading feedback (50.4 to 7.4; 30.0 to 1.2).
quoted_support: On Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, ExeCRE increases Pass@1 from 31.5 to 32.5 and reduces misleading feedback from 50.4 to 7.4.
